_comment: Copy to channels.json and edit for the channels you actually announce to. The script pairs each channel's constraints with the real release material; an assistant drafts from that, you approve and post each one, then `mark-announced`. Nothing here posts on its own. Add "active": false to any channel to pause it (kept here, skipped by `brief`).

channels.name: show-hn
channels.notes: Title <=80 chars, 'Show HN: <project> - <one-line>'. Link to the repo. The real pitch goes in your first comment: what it does, why it beats the obvious alternative, what's new in this release. No marketing voice.

channels.name: twitter-x
channels.notes: One hook + link. Lead with the single most interesting change in this release, not a feature list.

channels.name: reddit
channels.notes: Context-first, link in body not title. Self-promo gets downvoted; frame as 'here's a thing I built and what I learned', tied to the subreddit's interest.

channels.name: changelog-post
channels.notes: The why and the shape, grouped by theme. Mirror the project's CHANGELOG voice. Link each item to its PR/commit where useful.

channels.name: newsletter-blurb
channels.notes: 3-5 sentences a curator can drop in verbatim: what changed, why it matters, who it's for. No first person.
